history.rationale: reproducing test FAILS on buggy and PASSES on fixed; numerical probes are disabled (--no-probes), so the test transition is the whole of the evidence

plans.objective: Build both revisions identically as compiled pandas (Cython extensions), then run the developer-test cases from the two sparse test files on each revision, expecting failures on buggy and passes on fixed. Environment changes only; the developer tests stay untouched.
assumptions: The Python version is not stated in the context, so the harness default interpreter is used for both builds.
PR date is null, so no era-based pin is chosen; NumPy is left unbounded and only pinned if a removed API appears.
The native_library_failure diagnosis is read as meaning the compiled build step, not the test, needs attention; the plan rebuilds both revisions with compiled recipe as the single change.
Test case names are taken from the reproducing-test patch; the class name is unknown, so -k with the file path is used.

actions.step: Build buggy revision as a compiled package in its own venv, using the harness default interpreter (no pins; NumPy, dateutil, tzdata and Cython left unbounded since the context gives no constraint).
Build fixed revision with the same recipe and defaults so the comparison is like for like.
Run the test_array.py datetimelike cases on the buggy revision; the expected outcome is a genuine assertion failure, not a collection or import error.
actions.command: python -m pytest pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_array.py -k 'test_to_dense_datetimelike_non_numpy_fill or test_to_dense_datetimelike_fill_other_unit or test_array_object_datetimelike' -q

actions.step: Run the test_indexing.py datetimelike cases on the buggy revision.
Run the same test_array.py cases on the fixed revision; expected to pass.
